boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Appomattox Station record (April 8, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. Appomattox Court House (VA097) follows on April 9. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: The counts differ (four against three) and are preserved. The capture of Lee's supplies was created by the action.

open_questions: Custer's, Merritt's, Devin's and Crook's reports (Nos. 203, 200, 201, 208), Walker's and Pendleton's accounts (Pendleton No. 270), Lee's report of the attack on Walker's train (selected; cited under VA097) and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
